_source: Verified from decompiled alarm-notification-common-7.3.9 (…alarming.common.pipelines.*BlockProperties) and alarm-notification-gateway-7.3.9 (…alarming.pipelines.blocks.*Block, AlarmPipelineManagerImpl) in the decompiled jars. Registry = AlarmPipelineManagerImpl constructor registerBlockFactory(...) calls (9). Property keys, types, defaults and enums are the BasicProperty declarations in each *BlockProperties class; behaviour is each *Block.java. Cross-checked against a real data.bin round-tripped on a live 8.3.9 gateway. Nothing invented.

registry._cite: AlarmPipelineManagerImpl() lines ~114-122: registerBlockFactory(ExpressionBlock.FACTORY), EventStreamBlock, DelayBlock, NotificationBlock, SplitterBlock, SwitchBlock, JumpBlock, PropertySetterBlock, ScriptableBlock
registry.unknownFactoryBehaviour: AlarmPipelineManagerImpl: a block whose factoryId is blank or not in the registry is replaced by a NoOpBlock and logged 'Unknown block type'.

factoryId.purpose: one of registry.factoryIds; selects the block factory

blockId.purpose: unique within the pipeline; edge targets reference this. PipelineDescriptor.addBlock() assigns one if absent.

outputId.purpose: successor blockId for linear blocks. Missing/unknown -> synthetic NoOp terminal (path ends).

commonProperties._injectedAtLoad: The manager also sets dropoutConditions, fallbackPipeline and projectName onto every block config from the PipelineDescriptor before constructing the block.

delay.purpose: Hold the event for a fixed time, then transition. The wait is cancelled if the pipeline stops (or the event drops out).

expression.purpose: Evaluate an alarm expression to a boolean and branch. On evaluation error the event is routed to the pipeline's fallbackPipeline (or dropped).
Ignition alarm expression; coerced to boolean (bad quality => false)

trueOutput.purpose: successor blockId when the expression is true

falseOutput.purpose: successor blockId when the expression is false

switch.purpose: Evaluate an expression and route to the output whose table value matches (type-coerced compare); non-match -> _default_. On evaluation error -> fallbackPipeline.

mode.purpose: Designer editor mode (property picker vs free expression). The gateway evaluates 'expression' either way.

outputTable.purpose: ordered list of match values; entry i is paired with outputId{i}. Serialized as <arraylist><str>…</str></arraylist>.
outputTable._cite: SwitchBlockProperties.OUTPUT_TABLE; SwitchBlock.initialize() zips values.get(i) with BasicProperty("outputId"+i)

_default_._cite: SwitchBlockProperties.DEFAULT_CONDITION = "_default_"; SwitchBlock.initialize() 'this.catchAll = getOutputBlock(blockMap, new BasicProperty("_default_", UUID.class))'

splitter.purpose: Fan the event out to N parallel branches. Each branch gets a branched copy of the AlarmEvent; CommonAlarmProperties.LiveBranchCount is incremented by N.

outputId0..N-1._cite: SplitterBlock.initialize(): for i in 0..outputCount, getOutputBlock(blockMap, new BasicProperty("outputId"+i, UUID.class))

notification.purpose: Send the event to one or more notification profiles for each user on a roster, then transition. Honours user on-call schedules, optional throttling/consolidation, and a per-user pacing delay. Drops users mid-run per dropoutConditions.

notificationProfiles.purpose: profile names; blockVersion >=2. First profile that supports the user's contact type wins.

rosterType.purpose: 'roster' = 'roster' is a roster name or an expression yielding one; 'calculated' = 'roster' is an indented Jython calculateRoster(event, builder) body; 'Direct' = evaluate the roster once and notify all its users together (compared case-insensitively for Direct/calculated).

roster.purpose: roster name / roster-name expression / calculateRoster body per rosterType

ignoreSchedule.purpose: notify all roster users regardless of their on-call schedule / schedule adjustments

throttlingEnabled.purpose: aggregate/consolidate events (ThrottlingAggregator) before sending one notification for the batch

timeBetweenNotifications.purpose: pause between successive users on the roster; applied only after a user notification succeeds (a failure moves on immediately)

settingsFor_<profileName>.purpose: per-profile property overrides for this block; the profile sees ExtendedPropertySet.extend(blockConfig, thisPropertySet)

jump.purpose: Transfer the event to another pipeline in the same project. Destroys the current tracking context; a fresh one starts in the target pipeline. Terminal — has no output.

pipelineName.purpose: target pipeline name (resolved within the current project)

setProperty.purpose: Evaluate an expression and set the result as a property on the alarm event, then transition. Good-quality results only.

propertyId.purpose: name of the alarm-event property to set

scope.purpose: Global uses AlarmEventInstance.setGlobal (visible across Splitter branches); Local sets it on this branch's event only

script.purpose: Run arbitrary Jython against the event, then transition. Runs in the pipeline's project script scope.
indented body of 'def handleAlarm(event):' — 'event' is a PyAlarmEvent with an added cancelNotification() method. Compiled once at block init.

script.note: If outputId is unset the tracking context is destroyed (path ends) rather than falling to NoOp.

eventStream.purpose: Publish a JSON snapshot of the alarm event to an Event Stream resource in the project, then transition.

eventStreamName.purpose: path/name of the target Event Stream resource in the project. null -> logs an error and destroys the context.

message.purpose: declared property (EventStreamBlockProperties.MESSAGE); the gateway block publishes a fixed field set — eventId, source, displayPath, priority, priorityReadable, eventType, eventTypeReadable, eventFlags, eventTime.

syntheticTerminal.name: NoOpBlock
syntheticTerminal.purpose: Not user-placeable. AlarmPipelineManagerImpl adds one to every pipeline under a fixed random UUID. Any output edge that doesn't resolve to a real block lands here; it marks the tracking context complete and destroys it after 15 s. It is what 'the pipeline ends' means.
syntheticTerminal._cite: NoOpBlock; AbstractPipelineBlock.getOutputBlock() falls back to map.get(NoOpBlock.BLOCK_ID); AlarmPipelineManagerImpl: 'blocks.put(NoOpBlock.BLOCK_ID, new NoOpBlock(...))'

patterns.escalation: There is no Escalation block. Build one: Notification(roster A) -> Delay -> Expression('!{isAcked}') --true--> Notification(roster B) -> Delay -> … With the pipeline's dropoutConditions including OnAck, an acknowledgement anywhere pulls the event out of every downstream Delay/Notification automatically.
patterns.twoWayAck: There is no Two-Way / ACK block. Two-way = (1) a notification profile that can receive an ACK back (EmailNotificationProfileType two-way / POP3, or an SMS module's reply-to-ack) so the notified user can acknowledge from the message, plus (2) dropoutConditions containing OnAck so that ack stops the running pipeline. EmailNotificationProfile only appends the ACK link when two-way is enabled, an ACK is configured, and the event is not already acked.
patterns.consolidation: NotificationBlock.throttlingEnabled + throttlingDelay/throttlingFrequency (a debounce+max-rate window). Separately, OneWayNotificationProfile has its own consolidation settings at the profile level.
patterns.perPriorityRouting: Switch block, mode=Expression, expression '{priority}', outputTable ['Critical','High',...] -> different notification chains; '_default_' for the rest.
